note.announcementTitle: Board Meeting Outcome for Unaudited Standalone And Consolidated Financials Results For The Quarter And Half Year Ended September 30 2026
note.headline: Aerpace redirects Rs30cr of promoter-warrant proceeds from working capital to capex (Rs15cr) + debt repayment (Rs15cr), while standalone losses continue
thesisChain: Board approves variation in use-of-proceeds for the Rs48.825cr preferential warrant issue to N.K. Family Private Trust (Promoter Group), allotted 26-Sep-2026 per the 28-Sep-2026 note
Of the Rs36.62cr balance still receivable on warrant conversion, Rs30cr is re-allocated: Rs15cr to capex, Rs15cr to repayment of existing borrowings; remaining Rs6.62cr stays as working capital
Change requires shareholder approval (postal ballot/EGM) since it varies the original Offer Letter objects

Q2FY27 standalone results (same filing) show continued, OCR-degraded but directionally confirmed losses -- loss before tax widened versus the prior quarter and prior-year quarter -- so this is a loss-making company reallocating promoter capital toward capex and deleveraging rather than pure working capital

epsImpact.magnitude: no fresh capital raised -- this only redirects already-committed promoter proceeds; standalone P&L remains loss-making this quarter

note.insight: Formal Regulation 30 filing. This is a FOLLOW-UP to the 28-Sep-2026 note on the Rs48.825cr promoter-group warrant allotment (N.K. Family Private Trust) -- today's new information is a shareholder-approval-gated change in use of proceeds: Rs30cr of the Rs36.62cr still to be received on warrant conversion is being redirected from pure working capital to Rs15cr capex and Rs15cr debt repayment. The same filing's standalone Q2FY27 results are heavily OCR-garbled in the extracted text, but the figures that are legible indicate the standalone loss before tax widened versus both the immediately preceding quarter and the year-ago quarter, on a small (sub-Rs1.5cr) revenue base -- so this remains a loss-making micro-cap shifting promoter-funded capital toward capex and deleveraging. Watch the postal-ballot/EGM outcome and the next quarter's standalone numbers to see whether the capex spend narrows the loss.
